subject: Recap: Tool-calling integration patterns & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Tool-calling integration patterns & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of what we covered and suggested next steps so we have alignment on the integration approach for FinApps' virtual assistant use case: 

Summary of requirements from your side:
- Real-time account lookups and payments actions via backend microservices (low-latency).
- Guided workflows with structured outputs (forms + suggested next actions).
- Re-ranking of candidate responses using embeddings for contextual relevance.
- Multi-tool composition: transactional tools (payments), query tools (account search), and external APIs (KYC) that may run in parallel.

Redwood recommended approach (high-level):
1) SDK + Auth
   - Use Redwood JS/TS SDK (server-side) and authenticate with short-lived API keys + customer KMS for private deploys.
2) Tool/Function Calling Pattern
   - Define tools as typed function schemas (name, input_schema, output_schema, error_contract).
   - Choose tool executor: synchronous for quick lookups, async/background for long-running tasks (with polling/event webhooks).
   - Allow parallel calls for non-dependent tools (e.g., account search + scoring), then merge results with a deterministic policy.
3) Routing & Fallbacks
   - Route high-risk actions to a dedicated Dedicated capacity pool for SLAs; fall back to hosted model variant when unavailable.
4) Embeddings & Reranking
   - Use short, dense embeddings for candidate retrieval. Run a lightweight reranker model as a second-stage signal before tool selection.
5) Structured Output & Error Handling
   - Return JSON schema-validated payloads from model/tool chain. Propagate canonical error codes so client can present deterministic UI flows.

Attachments: redwood_tool_defs_v1.json (sample tool definitions + schemas), integration-maps.png (architecture sketch).

Proposed next steps:
- I can share a lightweight sample repo and postman collection for SDK + tool defs by EOD.
- Devs: can we schedule a 45-min technical sync this week to walk the sample tool definitions and auth flow? (Jonas / Dev please propose slots)
- Alex / Priya: confirm if we should include your payments team on the technical sync.

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Re: Recap: Tool-calling integration patterns & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications from our end: 

1) Auth: we prefer short-lived tokens and will use our existing OAuth 2.0 service. Is Redwood SDK compatible with token rotation + introspection?
2) Parallel tools: for payments we need strict serialization when doing balance checks -> payment to avoid double spend. We'll scope payments as a serial path; other tools (account search, KYC lookups) can be parallel.
3) Reranker: can you share recommended model sizes/latency tradeoffs for the reranker? Our latency SLO is 200ms P95 for the entire flow (excluding long-running background ops).

We want to include our payments eng lead (Sam Ortiz) on the technical sync. I'll send a calendar invite if the proposed slots work.

Best,
Alex
Product Manager | FinApps
alex.johnson@finapps.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finapps.com>
Cc: Priya Srinivasan <priya.s@finapps.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Tool-calling integration patterns & next steps

Alex — great notes. Short answers: 
- SDK & Auth: yes — Redwood SDK supports rotated short-lived tokens and can call your introspection endpoint. We'll share an auth sample (token rotation + introspection middleware) in the sample repo.
- Parallel vs Serial: agree on serializing the payment path. We'll provide a tool-def pattern that marks ordering constraints and a runtime-enforced execution graph.
- Reranker sizes: for P95 200ms budget we typically recommend a two-stage approach: a cheap dot-product embedding retrieval (vector DB) + a small cross-encoder reranker (e.g., 70M–200M) tuned for latency. On Dedicated capacity you can expect sub-200ms P95 for the rerank stage when batch sizes are small; we'll include benchmarks.

Attachments: redwood_tool_defs_v1.json (contains example tool schemas, marker for serial vs parallel, and sample error_contracts).

Proposed technical sync slots (PT):
- Thu 6/1 10:00–10:45
- Thu 6/1 15:00–15:45
- Fri 6/2 09:30–10:15

Jonas / Dev — can you confirm availability and whether you prefer a deeper architecture session (60m) or a short walkthrough (30–45m)?

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Re: Recap: Tool-calling integration patterns & next steps

Hi all —

I reviewed the sample tool defs quickly and a couple engineering notes before the sync: 
- For tool definitions, we'll include: name, description, input_schema (JSON Schema ref), output_schema, timeout_ms, concurrency_hint, idempotency_key_hint, and canonical_error_codes.
- For parallel execution, we should return a deterministic merge policy (priority order + timestamp) and include provenance metadata so the UI can show "source confidence" for suggested actions.
- Error handling: map runtime failures to 5 canonical categories: validation, auth, transient (retryable), permanent, and partial-success (e.g., some tools succeeded, one failed). Include an error_contract with suggested client UX patterns.

Also: Alex, can you confirm if your infra team prefers webhook notifications for async results or a polling endpoint? We'll implement both patterns in the sample.

I can take the deep architecture slot (60m) if you want to cover execution graph semantics + error contract examples.

-Dev
Senior Backend Engineer | Redwood Inference
